attempts.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 (AlmaLinux 9) as a 3-member MariaDB 10.5 Galera cluster (mariadb-server-galera + galera-26.4.22), with firewalld opened for 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568, /etc/hosts and galera.cnf (wsrep_on=ON, gcomm://node1,node2,node3, per-node address/name, rsync SST) on each node. Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, joined node2 and node3 via systemctl start mariadb, reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3 / Primary / Synced on all nodes. Verified multi-master write propagation (writes from each of the three nodes visible on all others), verified availability with one node down (stopped node3, cluster stayed Primary at size 2, write via node1 succeeded), and verified automatic resync on rejoin (node3 restarted, auto-rejoined, and caught up on the write made while it was down). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster health, issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot per node so the ack returned first, polled until reconnect, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed each node came back with cluster size 3 / Primary / Synced and all test rows intact before moving to the next node.
